attrs.title: Signs Performance Max isn’t working for you
attrs.lead: Performance Max is powerful, but easy to misread. These are the signs we see most, and what is usually behind them.

items.title: Most of its sales come from your brand name
items.text:
By default, Performance Max can show for searches of your own brand. Those people were already looking for you, so the sales would mostly have come anyway, but Performance Max reports them as its own and its return on ad spend looks excellent.

We split results into brand and non-brand, add brand exclusions and move brand searches into a separate, low-cost Search campaign. You then see what Performance Max really adds, and its budget goes to finding new customers.

items.title: One asset group for everything
items.text:
One asset group means one set of headlines, images and signals for every product and every audience. Google can’t tell a premium range from a clearance line, so the message is generic and a few products take most of the budget.

We build asset groups around product ranges, margins or audiences, each with its own copy, images, video and signals. Budget then follows the products and people that matter, not just the ones Google found first.

items.title: No video, so Google makes its own
items.text:
If you don’t add a video, Google builds one from your images and text. These auto-generated videos rarely look like your brand, and they run on YouTube in front of the very people you want to impress.

Our creative team makes short videos, images and copy for each asset group, sized for every placement. We test them against each other and replace the ones Google rates Low.

items.title: You can’t see which channels the money goes to
items.text:
Performance Max runs across Search, Shopping, YouTube, Display, Gmail and Maps, but the standard reports show one total. You can’t tell whether the budget goes to buyers on Search or to cheap Display placements.

Each month you get spend and results by channel, the search categories it showed for and the placements behind them. When one channel wastes money, we change the assets, signals or exclusions that feed it.

items.title: Lead campaigns bring poor leads
items.text:
For lead generation, Performance Max optimises for whatever you count as a conversion. If every form fill counts the same, it learns to find the cheapest form fills, which are often spam, students or people who will never buy.

We connect your CRM so Google learns which leads became customers, add lead values and filter out spam. Performance Max then aims for leads your sales team wants to call.

items.title: It competes with your Search campaigns
items.text:
Performance Max can take traffic from your own Search campaigns, often for your best keywords. Results move from one campaign to the other, costs rise and it’s hard to tell what’s working.

We set clear roles: Search for the keywords you want full control of, Performance Max for reach. Brand exclusions, negative keywords at account level and search themes keep the two from fighting.

attrs.label: How we set it up and run it
attrs.html:
How we set it up and run it

Good inputs first, then careful scaling. You see the plan and the first assets before anything goes live.

  1. We look at your current Performance Max results split by brand and non-brand, by channel and by product, and check the tracking, feed and assets that feed it. Most accounts have a few big leaks and a lot of missed potential.

    You get: A short audit with what to fix first.

    • Brand vs non-brand results split out
    • Channel and placement report from your data
    • Feed and Merchant Center checked
    • Conversion goals and values reviewed

  2. We plan the asset groups, the audience signals and the exclusions, and agree the goal: new customers, return on ad spend or qualified leads. Performance Max is only as good as the direction you give it.

    You get: A one-page campaign plan to approve.

    • Asset groups by range, margin or audience
    • Audience signals from your customer lists
    • Brand, URL and placement exclusions
    • Targets set from real results

  3. Our creative team makes the images, videos and headlines for each asset group. We set up the campaigns, fix the feed and check every conversion before launch.

    You get: Campaigns ready to launch, with your sign-off.

    • Images and videos for every placement
    • Headlines and descriptions per asset group
    • Feed titles, images and labels improved
    • Brand campaign set up alongside

  4. Performance Max needs a few weeks of steady data. We hold budgets and targets steady, watch the channel and search-category reports closely and step in only when something is clearly wrong.

    You get: A first-month report in plain English.

    • Budgets and targets held steady
    • Weekly checks on spend by channel
    • Search categories reviewed
    • Early asset ratings checked

  5. Each month we replace weak assets, refine signals and exclusions, move budget between asset groups and campaigns, and add new creative. You get a report and a call.

    You get: Steady gains, month after month.

    • New images and videos for weak assets
    • Budget moved to what works
    • New-customer and value goals tested
    • A monthly report and call

What we manage

Eight parts of Performance Max, managed every month

For each part: why it matters, what we do, what we usually find when we take over an account and what we change.

Area 1 of 8

Brand and exclusions

Without exclusions, Performance Max can spend on your brand name, your careers page or placements you’d never choose. Exclusions keep the budget on new customers.

What we do

  • Brand exclusion lists
  • A separate brand Search campaign
  • URL exclusions for blog, careers and support pages
  • Account-level negative keywords
  • Placement exclusions
  • Final URL expansion settings

What we often find

  • ! 41% of spend on people searching for the brand
  • ! Ads sending people to the careers page
  • ! Final URL expansion on with no exclusions
  • ! Ads in mobile games and parked domains

What we change

  • Brand exclusions, with brand moved to a low-cost Search campaign
  • URL exclusions for pages that don’t sell
  • Account-level negatives for job and free searches
  • Monthly placement review

Area 2 of 8

Asset groups

Asset groups decide which message goes with which products or audiences. Too few, and every product gets the same generic ad; too many, and each one has too little data to learn.

What we do

  • Asset groups by range, margin or audience
  • Listing groups for retail
  • Messages per asset group
  • Search themes
  • Budget share per group
  • Groups that should be merged or split

What we often find

  • ! One asset group for 1,840 products
  • ! Best-sellers and clearance lines treated the same
  • ! The same headlines in every group
  • ! No search themes

What we change

  • Groups by product range and margin
  • High-margin products in their own group
  • A clear message for each group
  • Search themes from your best Search keywords

Area 3 of 8

Creative: images, video and copy

Assets decide where your ads can show and how good they look there. Weak or missing assets push Performance Max into cheap placements and auto-generated video.

What we do

  • Images in every size
  • Short videos for YouTube and Shorts
  • Headlines and descriptions
  • Logos and brand guidelines
  • Asset ratings and performance
  • New creative each month

What we often find

  • ! Auto-generated video running on YouTube
  • ! 9 of 15 images rated Low
  • ! Headlines copied from the homepage
  • ! No new assets for over a year

What we change

  • Videos made by our team for each asset group
  • New images to replace Low-rated ones
  • Headlines written for each range or audience
  • A monthly creative refresh

Area 4 of 8

Audience signals

Signals tell Performance Max who to look for first. Without them it starts from scratch and takes longer to find the right people.

What we do

  • Customer lists
  • Website visitor lists
  • Custom segments from search terms
  • Interests and life events
  • Signals per asset group
  • New-customer acquisition goals

What we often find

  • ! No signals at all
  • ! The same signal on every asset group
  • ! Customer lists never uploaded
  • ! No new-customer goal, so it chases repeat buyers

What we change

  • Customer and visitor lists as signals
  • Custom segments built from your best search terms
  • Different signals per asset group
  • New-customer goals where they make sense

Area 5 of 8

Product feed

For retail, the feed is the ad. Titles, images, prices and labels decide which searches your products show for and how they look.

What we do

  • Titles with brand, type, size and colour
  • Images and extra images
  • Prices, sale prices and shipping
  • Custom labels for margin and best-sellers
  • Merchant Center errors and warnings
  • Products disapproved or limited

What we often find

  • ! Titles missing size, colour or brand
  • ! 212 products disapproved in Merchant Center
  • ! No custom labels, so margin can’t guide bidding
  • ! Images with text and watermarks

What we change

  • Titles rewritten with the words people search
  • Disapprovals fixed and monitored
  • Custom labels for margin, season and best-sellers
  • Clean product images

Area 6 of 8

Conversion goals and values

Performance Max chases whatever you count as a conversion. Wrong goals or missing values send it after the wrong customers.

What we do

  • Primary and secondary goals
  • Purchase values and currency
  • Lead values by type
  • Offline conversions from your CRM
  • Enhanced conversions
  • Double counting

What we often find

  • ! Newsletter sign-ups counted as primary
  • ! Purchase values including tax and shipping
  • ! Every lead counted the same
  • ! No offline conversions, so spam leads look good

What we change

  • Only real sales or qualified leads as primary goals
  • Correct values, without tax and shipping
  • Lead values from your CRM
  • Offline conversions uploaded daily

Area 7 of 8

Search categories and placements

Performance Max shows only a little of where it runs. We read the search categories and placement reports it does give, and act on them.

What we do

  • Search term insights and categories
  • Placements on Display and YouTube
  • Channel split
  • Brand vs non-brand results
  • Location and device results
  • Overlap with Search campaigns

What we often find

  • ! Search categories full of job and free searches
  • ! A third of spend on Display with few sales
  • ! Performance Max taking your best Search keywords
  • ! Results never split by channel

What we change

  • Negatives and search themes from the categories
  • Placement exclusions and better assets to steer channels
  • Clear roles for Search and Performance Max
  • A channel report every month

Area 8 of 8

Budgets and bidding

Performance Max needs steady budgets and realistic targets. Changing them too often resets learning; setting them too tight stops it spending.

What we do

  • Bid strategy and targets
  • Budget per campaign
  • Learning periods
  • Seasonality adjustments
  • Budget limits and lost share
  • Scaling plans

What we often find

  • ! A target return set far above anything achieved
  • ! Budgets changed every week
  • ! Best campaign limited by budget
  • ! No plan for seasonal peaks

What we change

  • Targets from real results, raised step by step
  • Changes made in planned steps
  • Budget moved to what works
  • Seasonality adjustments for sales and peaks

attrs.title: Why Performance Max disappoints
attrs.lead: The problems we see most often. Here is what each one looks like inside the account, and how we fix it.

items.title: Taking credit for brand searches
items.problem: Performance Max spends on people already searching for your brand and reports those sales as its own.
items.fix: Brand exclusions and a separate low-cost brand Search campaign, with results reported brand and non-brand.

items.title: Poor leads in lead generation
items.problem: Every form fill counts the same, so Performance Max finds the cheapest leads, many of them spam.
items.fix: Offline conversions and lead values from your CRM, and spam filtered out before it counts.

items.title: Auto-generated videos
items.problem: With no video added, Google builds its own from your images, and it runs on YouTube.
items.fix: Real videos made by our team for each asset group, refreshed every month.

items.title: One asset group for every product
items.problem: Every product shares one set of assets and signals, so a few best-sellers take the whole budget.
items.fix: Asset groups by range, margin or audience, each with its own message and signals.

items.title: Budget lost to Display
items.problem: A third of the budget goes to Display and Gmail placements that rarely sell.
items.fix: Better assets, placement exclusions and signals that steer spend to Search and Shopping.

Why they came to us

What changed
Brand moved to its own campaign, six asset groups by range and margin, videos made by our team. Sales to new customers grew while the budget stayed the same.

attrs.title: What it’s like to work with us
Performance Max Management questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: What is Performance Max?
items.answer: A Google Ads campaign type that runs across search, Shopping, YouTube, display, Gmail and Maps from one campaign, using Google’s automation.

items.question: Is Performance Max good for lead generation?
items.answer: It can be, if Google learns from lead quality, not just form fills. That means offline conversions or lead values from your CRM.

items.question: Why is Performance Max spending on my brand name?
items.answer: By default it can show on your brand searches, where people would have found you anyway. Brand exclusions stop that.

items.question: Can I see where Performance Max spends?
items.answer: Partly. Google shows channel results, search categories and some placements. We pull these into one monthly report.

items.question: Who makes the images and videos?
items.answer: Our own designers and video editors, for each asset group, with a refresh every month.

items.question: Performance Max or Search?
items.answer: Most accounts need both: search for control on key terms, Performance Max for reach.
